tasks.short: Identify prices and tabulate customer bills

steps.what: Identify prices by scanning goods or selecting service and admission items at the cash register
Resolve price exceptions and verify the tabulated bill before presenting the total

tasks.design: Keep the existing native price lookup and bill arithmetic in {OTHER}, the point-of-sale system. The cashier still identifies or scans items, resolves uncertain prices and checks the bill; existing automatic totals earn no new labour saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: The remaining human work is identifying the correct item and resolving exceptions rather than repeating register arithmetic.
tasks.enabler_now: Current native point-of-sale configuration already performs routine lookup and totals.
tasks.still_hard: Unlabelled items, conflicting promotions or unusual service requests require clarification.
tasks.human_edge: The cashier recognises when a displayed price does not represent the customer's actual purchase.
tasks.altitude: Cashier time and price-exception authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Match a customer request to the correct priced item

evidence.claim: Native point-of-sale lookup and totals are already part of a typical cashier workflow; existing system runtime is not a new human saving.

assumptions: Boundary is identifying prices and producing the checked bill, excluding payment receipt, inventory maintenance and customer policy explanations. Resolve overlapping item capture once across tasks.

Merchandise or service pricing owners produce catalogue identifiers, prices and promotion instructions through normal work. Cashier captures item identifiers, quantities and requested services in s1's 65 hours and checks exceptions within s2's 35 hours; no free structured basket or price override approval is assumed.

Missing identifiers or conflicting prices follow current manual clarification and authorized override routes; the proposal introduces no new pricing authority. Keep native configuration with no additional process or upkeep.
unknowns: Which exceptions consume the most cashier time
Whether any manual bill calculation actually remains
research_questions: How much time is scanning and exception handling rather than arithmetic already performed by the register?

already_counted.description: Identify items, capture quantities and resolve and check prices and the bill

incremental.description: No changed process or additional upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental upkeep=0. Native arithmetic already runs today; scanning and price-exception work retain their full time, so no additional saving is claimed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Answer incoming phone calls, establish the caller's purpose and connect them to appropriate help

tasks.design: Keep call reception and initial clarification human through {TELEPHONY}. The cashier establishes what the caller needs and answers or connects them through the current contact route.
tasks.previous_blocker: A caller's need may be unclear or require immediate personal help.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing native phone facilities already support answering and transfer.
tasks.still_hard: Misunderstood requests or unavailable colleagues require judgement and a helpful response.
tasks.human_edge: The cashier recognises confusion and helps the caller reach someone who can act.
tasks.altitude: Call-answering time and responsibility remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Call reception requires human clarification and routing in this unchanged workflow; no labour saving is claimed.

assumptions: Boundary is call reception, initial clarification and routing, excluding a separately owned substantive policy answer or transaction. Count the same conversation segment only once across tasks.
Caller produces the request after the phone is answered. Cashier elicits, verifies and captures relevant details within the retained 100 hours; no free structured intent or routing code is assumed.
Existing colleagues maintain normal contact information. Keep native phone facilities with no new bot, recording or capture process, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Call volumes and the range of caller needs
Which colleagues can receive transferred calls
research_questions: Do callers reach appropriate help without having to repeat essential details unnecessarily?

already_counted.description: Answer calls, clarify needs and connect callers to help

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental upkeep=0. Reception and clarification keep full time; substantive answers are counted separately without duplicating conversation effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Answer customer procedure and policy questions

steps.what: Understand customers' questions and clarify the procedure or policy context
Find current procedure or policy information relevant to the customer's question

loop.purpose: Locate relevant passages for uncommon wording of a policy question
loop.input: Cashier's clarified question and current published policy records
loop.output: Candidate passages with document version and section references, or no supported answer
loop.check: Cashier reads the original passages and checks scope, exceptions, effective date and fit to the customer's situation
loop.stop: One retrieval and one reformulated question; unsupported cases return to manual lookup or existing supervisor escalation
loop.why_not_simpler: Native search and fixed FAQ links are used first; the bounded loop is only for questions phrased differently from the documents

steps.what: Answer customers' questions and explain the relevant procedures or policies and their limits

tasks.design: Use native FAQ links and search in {DOCS} first, adding bounded passage retrieval only for differently phrased questions. The cashier checks the original policy and explains it personally, escalating unsupported or discretionary cases through the current route.
tasks.previous_blocker: A customer may describe a policy issue using words that do not match document headings.
tasks.enabler_now: Retrieval can suggest relevant source passages without making the customer's eligibility or exception decision.
tasks.still_hard: Policies can contain exceptions or leave discretion that a retrieved passage cannot settle.
tasks.human_edge: The cashier understands the customer's actual situation and explains an answer with appropriate limits.
tasks.altitude: At most a small lookup gain after checking; customer explanation and authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Explain terms and procedures in a customer's context

evidence.claim: The Albert Heijn vendor case combines fixed support flows with FAQ retrieval; it supports testing that approach, not a measured saving for cashier explanations.
The proposed passage-only workflow and very small net saving are unmeasured model scenarios.

assumptions: Boundary is the substantive customer policy question, excluding phone reception, processing returns, price overrides and supervisor decisions. Assign each conversation segment once.

Policy owners produce current documents with version, effective date and section identifiers through existing publication. Additional retrieval-source upkeep is counted below. Cashier captures the question and relevant context in s1's retained 35 hours; no free structured intent or eligibility code is assumed.

s2 retains 14 hours for source reading, scope checks and manual lookup exceptions. Missing sources, conflicting versions or uncertain applicability return to manual lookup or existing supervisor escalation; no unsupported answer is generated.

Try native FAQ configuration first and omit the loop if checking consumes the gain. s3 keeps full explanation time and grants no new exception authority; no autonomous customer-facing chatbot is introduced.
unknowns: Whether current policies have stable versions and accessible passages
Whether retrieval reduces lookup after checking source scope
research_questions: Does passage retrieval save any net time without misapplying exceptions to sample customer situations?

already_counted.description: Check retrieved policy passages and handle manual lookup exceptions

incremental.description: Maintain lookup instructions and audit unsupported passage suggestions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=94, gross=6; subtract 5 focal upkeep for central net=1. Range assumes native FAQs already cover most cases and passage checks consume most retrieval benefit. Two other-role upkeep hours are recorded separately; clarification and explanation keep full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Request information or assistance using the paging system and clarify the needed help

tasks.design: Keep help requests human through {OTHER}, the shop paging system. The cashier identifies the need and communicates enough context for the responsible colleague to respond.
tasks.previous_blocker: The need and urgency of assistance depend on what is happening at the till.
tasks.enabler_now: Current native paging facilities already support the request.
tasks.still_hard: A request may need discretion or clarification rather than a generic automatic alert.
tasks.human_edge: The cashier recognises the situation and asks for appropriate help.
tasks.altitude: Paging effort and responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Escalate a customer issue to an appropriate colleague

evidence.claim: Requesting assistance requires recognising a need and communicating it; no labour saving is claimed for replacing the cashier's request.

assumptions: Boundary is recognizing and issuing the help request, excluding the colleague's response, subsequent problem resolution and broader staff dispatch.

Cashier observes the situation and captures the needed information while making the request within the retained 100 hours. No free structured assistance or urgency flag is assumed; colleagues respond only after the request through unchanged work outside this task.
Keep current native paging conventions. No sensor, model or automated dispatch is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Which requests need a private rather than public channel
Who is responsible for responding to each request type
research_questions: Do pages convey the information needed for the right colleague to respond?

already_counted.description: Recognise the need, compose and issue a help request

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental upkeep=0. Recognition and communication retain full effort; colleague response time is outside the focal denominator.

role.altitude: Existing register arithmetic earns no additional saving; a tightly bounded policy lookup may help a little while service and judgement stay human.
reach: Learn request clarification and policy explanation from counter and rental clerks
skills_to_grow: Distinguish register output from verified item and price accuracy
Check policy scope before explaining it
Make concise requests for appropriate assistance
role.ambitious_version: Provide accurate, understandable customer help while using native records without overstating savings from automation already in place.
